item.title: Solved: How to Fix sqlalchemy.exc.NoSuchModuleError When Connecting to PostgreSQL
item.description:
In the process of setting up a connection to a PostgreSQL database using SQLAlchemy, you may encounter a frustrating error: sqlalchemy.exc.NoSuchModuleError: Can't load plugin: sqlalchemy.dialects:postgres. This can lead to numerous headaches as you try to troubleshoot your application. Let’s explore effective methods to resolve this issue and ensure your database connections are successful.

Key Reasons for sqlalchemy.exc.NoSuchModuleError

The root cause of this error often stems from changes made in SQLAlchemy version 1.4, specifically regarding dialect naming. The dialect previously known as postgres is now referred to as postgresql. While earlier versions may have continued to accept the postgres dialect with warnings, the updated version enforces this change.

item.title: Top 6 Methods to Resolve SQLAlchemy's TypeError: 'dict' Object Does Not Support Indexing
item.description:
When dealing with SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL, encountering the error message TypeError: 'dict' object does not support indexing can be quite frustrating. This issue often arises when executing SQL queries that involve the percentage LIKE operator. Below, I’ll detail various methods to diagnose and resolve this perplexing error.

Problem Overview

Consider the following hand-crafted SQL statement used to fetch data from a PostgreSQL database:

sql = """
 SELECT DISTINCT u.name FROM user u
 INNER JOIN city c ON u.city_id = c.id
 WHERE c.designation = upper('fantasy') 
 AND c.id IN (SELECT id FROM ref_geog WHERE short_name LIKE '%opt')
"""

Running this query throws an error, but substituting the wildcard with a direct match like short_name = 'helloopt' executes without issue. Attempts to escape the wildcard character by using %% yielded the same error.
